Score levers visible from the problem statement are (a) routing each destination along cheap paths, (b) sharing sub-paths so the source's data crosses each expensive edge at most once (redundancy reduction), (c) balancing load so per-network congestion/parallelism costs don't spike. strategies.title: [steiner-multicast] Global Steiner-tree multicast with shared-edge expansion
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: Steiner tree (global batch multicast approximation)
Replacement scope: replace the body of `search_algorithm`'s per-destination Dijkstra loop with a single global Steiner-tree construction plus path expansion into `BroadCastTopology`.
Compute budget: one `nx.algorithms.approximation.steinertree` call (O(V log V + E) per internal Dijkstra; terminals = 1 + len(dsts), typically ≤ 15) plus one BFS/shortest-path expansion pass. Evaluation time unchanged asymptotically.
Gain mechanism: the incumbent sends each destination independently along its own shortest path; expensive edges near the source are paid once per destination (times num_partitions). A Steiner tree forces shared trunks: expensive egress edges are paid once and the data fans out at cheap downstream branch nodes, which the per-destination construction cannot represent.
Plan: (1) Build a collapsed simple undirected view `S` from `G` where the weight of pair (u,v) is min over all parallel directed edges of their cost (skip cost=None edges, or treat as infinite, to stay conservative); keep a lookup `(u,v) -> actual cheapest directed edge data`. (2) Run `steiner_tree(S, [src] + dsts, weight='cost')`. (3) Convert the undirected tree to directed routes: for each tree node with a directed path from src in the tree, compute each destination's unique tree path from src; for consecutive nodes use the stored cheapest directed edge data `G[u][v]` (if the tree used the reverse direction, take the cheapest directed edge in that direction from the original graph). (4) For each dst, for each partition j, `append_dst_partition_path(dst, j, [s, t, G_edge_data])` exactly as the incumbent does — preserving the output format and validity. (5) Fallback: if `steiner_tree` raises or any dst path is missing in `G`, fall back to the incumbent's per-dst Dijkstra for that dst only. Validity preserved because every appended hop is a real directed edge of `G` and every (dst, partition) slot gets a full src→dst chain. strategies.title: [free-link-routing] Route through unpriced (cost=None) links treated as zero-cos
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: unpriced-edge exploitation via Dijkstra on a reweighted graph
Replacement scope: replace the incumbent's single `nx.dijkstra_path(h, src, dst, weight="cost")` call inside the per-dst loop with a two-candidate comparison: Dijkstra on a copy where cost=None edges are reweighted to 0.
Compute budget: one extra graph copy + one extra Dijkstra per destination; negligible evaluation-time effect.
Gain mechanism: `make_nx_graph` explicitly reports "no_cost_pairs" — directed edges that exist with throughput but `cost=None`. The incumbent's Dijkstra will crash or misbehave on None weights in general, and certainly never deliberately routes through them. If the evaluator bills None as 0 or skips unpriced edges in cost accounting, these are free transfers the incumbent cannot use.
Plan: (1) After removing src in-edges and self-loops, build `h_free = h.copy()`; for every edge with `data["cost"] is None`, set `data["cost"] = 0.0`. (2) For each dst, compute candidate A = Dijkstra path on `h_free`, candidate B = Dijkstra path on `h` (with None replaced by a large sentinel like 1e9 so None edges are avoided). (3) Score each candidate by summing `G[u][v]["cost"] if not None else 0.0` along the path; pick the cheaper. (4) Emit the winner with the incumbent's exact append loop over partitions, using the real edge data from `G`. strategies.title: [per-partition-disjoint] Diversify partitions across k-cheapest parallel routes
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: k-shortest-path partition diversification (per-partition routing over distinct parallel networks)
Replacement scope: replace the incumbent's "same Dijkstra path for all partitions" emission loop with per-partition path selection from the k cheapest distinct simple paths.
Compute budget: `nx.shortest_simple_paths(h, src, dst, weight="cost")` truncated at k = num_partitions paths per destination (bounded generator consumption); evaluation-time effect is a small constant factor over incumbent.
Gain mechanism: the incumbent routes all num_partitions copies of the data over the identical path, concentrating full volume on each edge of that path. If the evaluator's cost is charged per (edge, partition) with congestion-dependent or per-network pricing, spreading partitions across the k cheapest edge-distinct paths exploits the multigraph's parallel networks — a degree of freedom (per-partition route choice) the incumbent structurally fixes to a constant.
Plan: (1) Precompute for each dst the generator `shortest_simple_paths(h, src, dst, weight="cost")` (with None costs replaced by sentinel 1e9 in a copy `h_w`). (2) Take the first k = num_partitions distinct-cost paths; if fewer exist, repeat the cheapest path to fill remaining partitions (preserving validity — every partition must reach dst). (3) Assign partition j to candidate path j (optionally re-ranked so the overall most expensive path carries the fewest partitions when k > num_partitions). (4) Emit each partition's path with the same `[s, t, G[s][t]]` edge-data format. (5) Hard validity: every emitted path is a genuine simple src→dst path in `G`; every (dst, partition) slot is filled. Fallback: if the generator errors, emit the incumbent's single Dijkstra path for all partitions. Expected-gain check: under any evaluator whose per-edge charge saturates or scales with per-edge load (throughput attribute exists on every edge precisely to model this), moving ≥1 partition off the shared cheapest path to the 2nd-cheapest strictly reduces peak edge load — falsifiable by total_cost strictly below 1035.14; if cost is purely linear per GB per partition, this strategy performs no worse than the incumbent by construction (cheapest path still fills the majority of partitions).

strategies.title: [per-dst-hybrid] Per-destination min of Steiner-tree path vs. individual shortes
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: steiner-refinement (per-dst hybrid selection)
Replacement scope: the destination-expansion loop in `search_algorithm` (the block after the BFS tree-path computation that unconditionally uses the tree path per dst).
Compute budget: one Dijkstra per destination on the collapsed graph (already computed implicitly) plus one `nx.shortest_simple_paths` generator limited to ≤10 paths per dst; no new optimizer starts. Evaluation-time effect negligible.
Gain mechanism: the Steiner tree minimizes *total* edge cost, which can force individual destinations onto detours that are more expensive than their own cheapest unicast path — the incumbent pays that detour for all `num_partitions` copies. The new degree of freedom is per-dst arbitration: for each destination, compute both (a) the tree-path cost (sum of directed-edge costs, None→0) and (b) the cost of its cheapest direct shortest path (and optionally the next few k-shortest simple paths), then emit whichever is cheaper, reusing the tree only where it actually helps that destination. Because the tree was built on shared edges, destinations that keep tree paths still enjoy sharing; destinations that defect take their cheaper private route. This strictly dominates the incumbent on any instance where a tree path is not individually cheapest, and never does worse (the incumbent's tree path is one of the compared candidates). Path continuity is preserved by construction: every emitted hop is validated as a real directed edge of `h`, with the existing per-dst Dijkstra fallback kept for unreachable/broken cases; all `dsts` still receive all `num_partitions` partitions.
Expected-gain check: whenever any destination's cheapest unicast path costs less than its Steiner-tree path (a routine occurrence with a 2-approximation tree), the emitted plan's summed edge cost strictly drops below the incumbent's `total_cost` of 693.10 while validity is bit-identical in structure, so `cost_score` must improve if the evaluator bills per emitted hop.

strategies.title: [marginal-cost-partition] Incremental edge pricing across partitions and destina
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: marginal-cost-partition
Replacement scope: the entire route-emission logic of `search_algorithm` (replace the single global tree + per-dst copy with an incremental-cost greedy pass), keeping `BroadCastTopology` and the Dijkstra fallback untouched.
Compute budget: per (dst, partition) pair, enumerate ≤10 shortest simple paths (`nx.shortest_simple_paths`, early-break after 10) on the None→0 cost graph; ≤ `len(dsts) × num_partitions × 10` Dijkstra-like expansions, no iterative optimizer. Evaluation-time effect: small linear factor.
Gain mechanism: the incumbent prices every (dst, partition) route independently at full edge cost, so an edge reused by all 4 partitions of all dsts is charged per copy with no discount. The new degree of freedom is a *marginal pricing ledger*: maintain `paid[(u,v)]` = cost already incurred on that directed edge; when choosing a route for the next (dst, partition), score candidate paths by `sum(cost(e) if e not in paid else 0)` so edges already paid for are free, then add the chosen path's full edge costs to the ledger. Process pairs in order of decreasing standalone path cost (largest payers first, so later cheap takers can piggyback). This explicitly models edge sharing that neither the Steiner tree (which optimizes a single shared structure, not per-partition copies) nor per-dst Dijkstra can realize, and it never emits a route costlier than the plain-Dijkstra incumbent (which is the first candidate considered for the first partition). All candidate paths are real directed paths in `h`, guaranteeing continuity; every dst still gets all partitions, and unreachable dsts fall back exactly as today.
Expected-gain check: if the evaluator charges each emitted hop's cost (as `cost_score` from `total_cost` implies), any edge appearing in ≥2 emitted routes yields a strictly positive cost reduction the incumbent cannot express, so total emitted cost < 693.10 on at least one of the 5 benchmark configs; if no such overlap exists the plan degenerates to the incumbent and scores identically, making the threshold falsifiable.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: throughput-aware-flow
Replacement scope: the graph-collapsing + route-selection core of `search_algorithm` (the `S` construction, the `steiner_tree` call, and the path-expansion block), replaced by a min-cost-flow formulation with per-edge throughput-derived capacities.
Compute budget: one `nx.network_simplex` solve per instance on the collapsed directed graph with `num_partitions` units of demand at a super-sink; node/edge counts are ≤ a few hundred, so a single solve per run, no multistart. Evaluation-time effect: seconds at most.
Gain mechanism: `make_nx_graph` attaches a `throughput` to every edge, and the incumbent ignores it entirely. If the evaluator's cost includes congestion/parallelism (e.g., transfer time or cost penalties when flow approaches link capacity, or per-network pricing that saturates), the plan must spread `num_partitions` units across parallel same-pair links instead of stacking them on the single cheapest edge. Construct a flow network: super-sink connected from each dst with capacity `num_partitions`, capacities = per-edge `throughput`, costs = edge `$cost` (None→0, but with a tiny positive epsilon like 1e-6 so the simplex prefers capacity-feasible cheap links over unpriced ones when both are saturated); demand = `num_partitions` per dst. Extract, for each dst and partition, one unit of flow as a connected src→dst path by walking the positive flow decomposition; each unit's hops are real directed edges, guaranteeing continuity; per-dst Dijkstra fallback covers any dst the flow solve fails to satisfy. This is a genuinely different construction (flow decomposition with capacities) rather than another spanning-tree heuristic, and it is the only candidate that can exploit the multi-network parallel edges the problem statement highlights.

strategies.plan:

Mechanism family: milp-directed-steiner
Replacement scope: Add as a fourth seed generator inside `search_algorithm`, parallel to Candidates A/B/C, before the seed-argmin commitment; keep `local_search`, `sp_cost`, and all append/fallback logic untouched.
Compute budget: Only run when |W.edges| ≤ 1500 and |reachable| ≤ 12 (skip silently otherwise, so no risk on large configs); one `scipy.optimize.milp` (HiGHS) solve with a hard node/time cap of 60s via `options`/limited variables; if scipy is missing, MILP_ERROR, or the solve is infeasible/suboptimal, fall through to the existing seeds. Evaluation-time effect: one LP solve on small graphs, zero on large ones.
Gain mechanism: New optimized subsystem — exact global optimum instead of heuristic structure: binary variable x_e for each directed edge in W, continuous flow f_e^{(t)} per terminal per edge, constraints: src flow 1, dst sink −1, other nodes conserve, f_e^{(t)} ≤ x_e, minimize Σ cost_e · x_e (free/None edges at 0). This directly encodes *edge sharing across all destinations simultaneously* — the exact objective `sp_cost` measures — and can find optimal unions (e.g. a high-cost trunk edge worth buying for 2 of 5 dsts while 3 others route independently) that neither SPH growth, hub chains, SPT, nor the monotone local search can reach from any seed. Convert the optimal x_e support to per-dst routes via `routes_from_edges` verification, feed as a seed to the unchanged `local_search` (which only polishes), commit the argmin over all seeds including the incumbent's — so the result is ≤ incumbent whenever the MILP seed is no better, and strictly better when the exact optimum beats 627.12. Validity: routes come only from real directed edges of `W`/`h` with hop verification and the existing per-dst Dijkstra fallback for unmodeled dsts; infeasible/unbounded cases never reach the output.
Expected-gain check: the MILP minimizes the exact same union-edge-cost objective that `sp_cost` evaluates, so when it solves its cost is a certified lower bound on what any seed-based heuristic can achieve — strictly below the incumbent's `total_cost` of 627.12 whenever any heuristic slack remains; falsifiable threshold: `total_cost < 627.11` on at least one MILP-solved config with `runs_successfully = 1`.

strategies.title: [coordinated-subtree-graft] Multi-destination subtree grafting move inside the e
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: coordinated-subtree-graft
Replacement scope: The move loop inside `local_search(seed_routes)` in `search_algorithm` — keep the two existing moves, add a third coordinated move; seeds, SPH, hub, and SPT stages unchanged.
Compute budget: At most 3 sweeps (as now); the new move is bounded to at most |reachable|² junction candidates per sweep, each evaluated by O(1) dictionary lookups into the already-precomputed `pair_path` and an O(total path length) `sp_cost` call. No new Dijkstras. Expected evaluation-time effect: negligible change (<10% runtime increase).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's moves re-route **one destination at a time**. Once the solution sits at a local optimum, no single-dst substitution can improve because moving any one path off a shared edge abandons the sharing benefit, even though moving **two or more destinations together** onto a different shared trunk would pay for itself. The new degree of freedom is a coordinated multi-dst move: pick a junction node `j` on some existing path, take the set `D(j)` of all destinations whose current path passes through `j`, and re-route the *entire group* simultaneously to a new common suffix `pair_path[(j', d)]` from a different junction `j'` reached by a prefix of another existing path (or re-route the group from `src` directly via a fresh group-Dijkstra on the marginal graph where edges used by ≥2 group members are priced 0). Accept only if the union `sp_cost` strictly decreases (or a plateau budget of ≤2 equal-cost accepts per sweep, as now). This move can escape the single-dst plateau because the shared trunk cost is split across all group members in one evaluation, which no sequence of incumbent moves can propose without passing through a worse intermediate state. Hard validity is preserved: every candidate path is verified hop-by-hop against `h.has_edge` exactly as the incumbent does, and the per-dst Dijkstra fallback for unreachable dsts is untouched.
Expected-gain check: the incumbent's own run log states both committed structures plateaued at equal cost with single-dst moves; the group move is a strict superset of the incumbent's move set, so the local optimum it reaches has union cost ≤ 627.12 and, because it can traverse improving multi-dst transitions the incumbent cannot, any strictly lower plateau found on any of the 5 configs raises `combined_score` above 0.001592 (falsifiable: if no config improves, the group move found no improving transition and the score stays 0.001592).

strategies.title: [wong-dual-ascent] Directed-Steiner dual-ascent construction with reduced-cost p
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: wong-dual-ascent
Replacement scope: The Candidate-A SPH multistart block (`sph(terminal_order)` and its 10 orderings) is replaced by a Wong-style dual-ascent construction that produces both a primal arborescence and a reduced-cost graph; Candidates B/C, `local_search`, and all fallbacks stay unchanged, and the dual-ascent tree simply enters `seeds` alongside them.
Compute budget: One dual-ascent pass = at most |reachable| rounds, each doing one multi-source Dijkstra on `W` (bounded, same cost as one SPH round). Optionally 3 dual-ascent runs with different initial terminal orderings. This is strictly cheaper than the current 10-order SPH multistart it replaces. Expected evaluation-time effect: neutral to faster.
Gain mechanism: SPH is a purely greedy primal heuristic with no optimality information; Wong's dual-ascent for directed Steiner trees iteratively raises shortest-path-based dual variables on terminal subsets, and (a) the edges that remain with zero reduced cost form a sparse subgraph in which the true optimum provably lives, and (b) running the primal path-attachment greedy *on the reduced-cost graph* (zero-reduced-cost edges priced 0, others at reduced cost) yields trees SPH cannot construct — it systematically prefers edges the dual certificate identifies as under-priced. Concretely: maintain dual potentials `y(S)` for terminal subsets; each round, for every unconnected terminal `t`, find its shortest path from the current root set in the reduced-cost graph, raise the dual on the blocking cut until some edge saturates, add the saturated edge's endpoint set to the root set; repeat until all terminals connect. The resulting edge set is expanded into per-dst routes with the existing `routes_from_edges`, validated with `h.has_edge`, costed with `sp_cost`, and pushed as an additional seed into the existing best-of-seeds `local_search`, which is monotone — so the committed plan can only match or beat the current 627.12. Additionally, the final dual objective is a certified lower bound on the optimal union cost; if it equals the primal cost on any config, that config is provably optimal and further search there is wasted (a bottleneck-diagnosis the incumbent completely lacks). Hard validity: unchanged — the tree routes pass through the same hop-verification and per-dst Dijkstra fallback.
Expected-gain check: dual-ascent's reduced-cost greedy explores a different construction basin than all 10 SPH orderings (which the run log shows have plateaued), and since `local_search` is monotone and the incumbent seeds are retained, the new seed can only lower the 627.12 total or leave it equal — falsifiable threshold: if the dual bound equals 627.12 on all 5 configs the score stays 0.001592 and the family is exhausted.

strategies.title: [backward-terminal-merge] Grow the multicast tree from the destination side towa
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: backward-terminal-merge
Replacement scope: Adds a Candidate-D construction alongside (not replacing) Candidates A/B/C; the seed selection and `local_search` stages are reused verbatim, and the SPH multistart may be trimmed to its 2 deterministic orderings to pay for the new stage.
Compute budget: One construction = at most |reachable| merge rounds, each a single multi-source Dijkstra on the reversed graph `W_rev` (edge (u,v) → (v,u), same cost), so the total is bounded by the SPH stage it is budgeted against. Expected evaluation-time effect: neutral.
Gain mechanism: All incumbent constructions grow **forward from the source**, attaching terminals one at a time by cheapest path from the already-connected set. In cloud egress graphs, directed costs are strongly asymmetric (egress from a provider is priced, ingress often free/`None`), so the cheapest way to *reach* a destination is not the cheapest way to be *reached from* it: growing backward from the destinations on the reversed graph and merging terminal clusters toward `src` produces merge points and shared trunks that forward growth never considers — e.g., two destinations whose cheap free-ingress edges converge on a common relay that is expensive to leave forward but free to enter backward. Concretely: start each terminal as its own cluster root; repeatedly run multi-source Dijkstra on `W_rev` from all cluster roots, find the cheapest connection of any cluster to another cluster or to `src`, merge, and stop when one cluster contains `src` and all terminals; convert the reversed arborescence into forward per-dst routes (each reversed edge is a real forward edge in `h`), verify hops, cost with `sp_cost`, and feed as a fourth seed into the unchanged monotone `local_search`. Because the incumbent seeds are retained and the local search never increases cost, the committed plan weakly dominates the current 627.12; the gain comes exclusively from the new backward-merge topology, a contact direction none of the 10 forward SPH orderings, the hub chains, or the SPT can realize. Hard validity: identical verification and fallback path as incumbent.
Expected-gain check: the backward construction's trees differ structurally from every incumbent seed whenever reversed and forward shortest-path structures disagree (guaranteed on asymmetric-cost graphs like this one, where `None`-cost ingress edges exist), so it supplies a genuinely new starting basin to the monotone local search — falsifiable threshold: if the resulting best-of-seeds cost equals 627.12 on all 5 configs, no config's cost structure rewards backward merging and the score stays 0.001592.

strategies.title: [free-scc-contraction] Contract zero-cost strongly-connected components into sup
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: free-scc-contraction
Replacement scope: Replace the construction of the routing graph `W` and the seed-generation phase (Candidates A/B/C) inside `search_algorithm`; keep `sp_cost`, `local_search`, `dijkstra_route` fallback, and the final path-emission block unchanged.
Compute budget: One SCC computation (Tarjan, O(V+E)) plus one Steiner/SPH run on the contracted graph (contracted graph is strictly smaller than `W`). No new optimizer starts beyond the incumbent's 10 SPH orderings; per-start work is on the contracted graph, so evaluation time decreases or stays flat.
Gain mechanism: The graph contains many `cost=None` pairs (make_nx_graph prints them explicitly). The incumbent prices them at 0 per edge but still forces routing to traverse them one hop at a time and, critically, its Steiner/SPH search wastes effort exploring inside free regions and can attach terminals through priced detours when a free path exists. Contracting each SCC of the zero-cost subgraph into a single supernode makes every intra-SCC traversal literally free and unconditional, so all search effort concentrates on the priced boundary edges — the only edges that matter to cost. Terminals in the same free SCC as the source become zero-cost by construction, a state the incumbent can only reach accidentally.
Plan: (1) Build subgraph F of `h` containing only edges with `cost is None`; compute SCCs of F. (2) Build contracted digraph C: each SCC is a node; for every priced edge (u,v) of `W`, add C-edge (scc(u), scc(v)) with the min cost over all such cross edges (keep a map back to the cheapest real edge). Source maps to its SCC; each dst maps to its SCC. (3) Run the incumbent's directed SPH multistart (10 orderings) on C over the mapped terminal set, plus the SPT seed; verify and expand: a path in C expands to a real node path by inserting, for each contracted hop (A→B), the cheapest real priced edge from any node in A to any node in B, and inside each SCC a free directed path (BFS on F) between the entry and exit nodes. (4) Feed expanded per-dst paths through the existing `sp_cost`/`local_search` machinery; commit the best. Validity: every emitted hop is a real edge of `h`; per-dst Dijkstra fallback still covers any dst whose expansion fails, so all dsts always receive a path.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is unconditional free traversal inside zero-cost SCCs; whenever any incumbent path uses a priced edge whose endpoints lie in one free SCC (or a priced edge replaceable by a free intra-SCC detour), the contracted solution strictly lowers raw `total_cost` below 627.12, hence raises `combined_score` above 0.001592 — falsifiable by rerunning the same 5 configs.

strategies.title: [recursive-dst-bisection] Split the destination set into sub-multicasts with ind
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: recursive-dst-bisection
Replacement scope: Replaces the single global seed-generation block (Candidates A/B/C) with a divide-and-conquer seed generator; `local_search`, `sp_cost`, and the emission/fallback blocks are reused verbatim.
Compute budget: At most 2^⌈log2|dsts|⌉ SPH calls total across the recursion (each leaf and internal node runs one SPH on ≤10 orderings as today — cap recursion depth at 3, i.e., splits into at most 8 groups); expected evaluation-time increase is bounded by ~3× the incumbent's seed phase.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent forces ONE shared tree for all destinations. When the destination set splits into geographically separated clusters (typical: one cloud provider's regions are cheap to reach from each other but inter-provider trunk edges are expensive), a single Steiner tree pays for spurious connecting edges between clusters, while per-dst shortest paths pay trunk edges repeatedly. The optimum is often a small number (2–4) of independent sub-trees. Neither the incumbent's seeds (one global tree, hub chains, SPT) nor its local moves (single-dst reroute, prefix splice) can decompose the destination set — the move class has no operator that splits a tree.
Plan: (1) Cluster `reachable` by running SPH once on the full set and cutting the resulting arborescence at its 2–3 highest-cost edges (or, equivalently, k-means-style grouping by pairwise shortest-path distances in `W`, k ∈ {2,3,4}); alternatively split by sorted src-distance into contiguous halves, depth ≤ 3. (2) For each candidate partition of dsts into groups, run directed SPH per group (reusing the incumbent's `sph` and `routes_from_edges` verbatim) to get one sub-tree per group; union the per-group per-dst paths. (3) Also evaluate a "shared trunk" variant: cheapest group's path from src reused as prefix for other groups. (4) Score every candidate partition with `sp_cost` (union cost — edges shared across groups still counted once), keep the best as an additional seed alongside the incumbent's seeds, run `local_search` on all seeds, commit the argmin. Deterministic: all partitions enumerated from a fixed depth-3 bisection tree, no RNG. Validity: each group's routes are verified hop-by-hop against `h` exactly as today; ungrouped/unreachable dsts fall back to `dijkstra_route`.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the partition of the terminal set into independent arborescences; the incumbent's single-tree representation cannot express it, and any config where the optimal multicast is disconnected (inter-cluster trunk cost exceeds intra-cluster savings) yields `total_cost` strictly below 627.12 — falsifiable by comparing per-config union costs on the 5 benchmark configs.

strategies.title: [lp-sharing-pipage] LP relaxation of the edge-sharing multicast with determinist
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: lp-sharing-pipage
Replacement scope: Adds a fourth candidate-seed generator alongside A/B/C in `search_algorithm` (the seed-selection and `local_search` phases are unchanged); the LP is solved only on a reduced candidate-edge set.
Compute budget: One LP per config on the reduced edge set (candidate edges = union of per-dst shortest paths and the incumbent's best tree, typically O(|dsts|·diameter) edges), solved via a bounded number (≤200) of simplex/dual-ascent iterations or scipy.linprog if available, with a hard fallback to skipping the candidate on any solver failure; pipage rounding is O(candidates × |dsts|). Evaluation-time increase is bounded by roughly one extra seed's local search.
Gain mechanism: The true objective — union cost of per-dst paths, each edge charged once — is a submodular set-cover-like problem. All incumbent seeds are combinatorial constructions that commit to a tree before knowing the global trade-off; an LP relaxation over edge-usage variables (x_e ∈ [0,1] shared across all dsts, flow constraints per dst) gives a fractional optimum that lower-bounds the incumbent's achievable cost and, via pipage rounding (deterministic, cost-monotone in the rounded variable), yields an integral solution with a provable approximation factor the incumbent lacks. Pipage rounding never increases the fractional objective, so the seed is guaranteed at or near the LP bound — a certificate-based starting point none of the combinatorial seeds can promise.
Plan: (1) Build reduced digraph R from candidate edges: all edges on each dst's k=1 shortest path in `W`, all edges of the incumbent's best tree, and all edges on shortest paths between terminal pairs (reuse `pair_path`). (2) LP variables: f_e ≥ 0 per dst (flow) plus shared indicator y_e ≥ f_e for every dst, minimize Σ c_e·y_e subject to per-dst unit flow conservation from src to dst on R. Solve with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) if importable; otherwise implement a simple dual-ascent on the LP (bounded 200 iterations) — on failure, return no seed. (3) Pipage rounding: repeatedly pick the y_e closest to 1/2, deterministically round up if its marginal union-cost contribution is ≤ fractional cost, else down, repairing per-dst connectivity with Dijkstra on the rounded edge set (edges with y_e=1 priced 0). (4) Emit per-dst paths from the rounded edge set via `routes_from_edges`, verify against `h`, add as a seed to the existing best-of-seeds `local_search`. Validity: rounded solution is a real directed path set verified hop-by-hop; failure at any stage silently drops the seed, leaving all incumbent seeds intact.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is a fractional global optimum over all dsts simultaneously with a monotone rounding guarantee; if the incumbent's committed cost 627.12 exceeds the LP lower bound on any config (typical for combinatorial 2-approximation seeds), the rounded seed strictly lowers `total_cost` and raises `combined_score` above 0.001592 — falsifiable by printing the LP bound per config.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [recursive-dst-bisection] Split the destination set into sub-multicasts with ind
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: recursive-dst-bisection
Replacement scope: Replaces the single global seed-generation block (Candidates A/B/C) with a divide-and-conquer seed generator; `local_search`, `sp_cost`, and the emission/fallback blocks are reused verbatim.
Compute budget: At most 2^⌈log2|dsts|⌉ SPH calls total across the recursion (each leaf and internal node runs one SPH on ≤10 orderings as today — cap recursion depth at 3, i.e., splits into at most 8 groups); expected evaluation-time increase is bounded by ~3× the incumbent's seed phase.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent forces ONE shared tree for all destinations. When the destination set splits into geographically separated clusters (typical: one cloud provider's regions are cheap to reach from each other but inter-provider trunk edges are expensive), a single Steiner tree pays for spurious connecting edges between clusters, while per-dst shortest paths pay trunk edges repeatedly. The optimum is often a small number (2–4) of independent sub-trees. Neither the incumbent's seeds (one global tree, hub chains, SPT) nor its local moves (single-dst reroute, prefix splice) can decompose the destination set — the move class has no operator that splits a tree.
Plan: (1) Cluster `reachable` by running SPH once on the full set and cutting the resulting arborescence at its 2–3 highest-cost edges (or, equivalently, k-means-style grouping by pairwise shortest-path distances in `W`, k ∈ {2,3,4}); alternatively split by sorted src-distance into contiguous halves, depth ≤ 3. (2) For each candidate partition of dsts into groups, run directed SPH per group (reusing the incumbent's `sph` and `routes_from_edges` verbatim) to get one sub-tree per group; union the per-group per-dst paths. (3) Also evaluate a "shared trunk" variant: cheapest group's path from src reused as prefix for other groups. (4) Score every candidate partition with `sp_cost` (union cost — edges shared across groups still counted once), keep the best as an additional seed alongside the incumbent's seeds, run `local_search` on all seeds, commit the argmin. Deterministic: all partitions enumerated from a fixed depth-3 bisection tree, no RNG. Validity: each group's routes are verified hop-by-hop against `h` exactly as today; ungrouped/unreachable dsts fall back to `dijkstra_route`.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the partition of the terminal set into independent arborescences; the incumbent's single-tree representation cannot express it, and any config where the optimal multicast is disconnected (inter-cluster trunk cost exceeds intra-cluster savings) yields `total_cost` strictly below 627.12 — falsifiable by comparing per-config union costs on the 5 benchmark configs.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [free-scc-contraction] Contract zero-cost strongly-connected components into sup
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: free-scc-contraction
Replacement scope: Replace the construction of the routing graph `W` and the seed-generation phase (Candidates A/B/C) inside `search_algorithm`; keep `sp_cost`, `local_search`, `dijkstra_route` fallback, and the final path-emission block unchanged.
Compute budget: One SCC computation (Tarjan, O(V+E)) plus one Steiner/SPH run on the contracted graph (contracted graph is strictly smaller than `W`). No new optimizer starts beyond the incumbent's 10 SPH orderings; per-start work is on the contracted graph, so evaluation time decreases or stays flat.
Gain mechanism: The graph contains many `cost=None` pairs (make_nx_graph prints them explicitly). The incumbent prices them at 0 per edge but still forces routing to traverse them one hop at a time and, critically, its Steiner/SPH search wastes effort exploring inside free regions and can attach terminals through priced detours when a free path exists. Contracting each SCC of the zero-cost subgraph into a single supernode makes every intra-SCC traversal literally free and unconditional, so all search effort concentrates on the priced boundary edges — the only edges that matter to cost. Terminals in the same free SCC as the source become zero-cost by construction, a state the incumbent can only reach accidentally.
Plan: (1) Build subgraph F of `h` containing only edges with `cost is None`; compute SCCs of F. (2) Build contracted digraph C: each SCC is a node; for every priced edge (u,v) of `W`, add C-edge (scc(u), scc(v)) with the min cost over all such cross edges (keep a map back to the cheapest real edge). Source maps to its SCC; each dst maps to its SCC. (3) Run the incumbent's directed SPH multistart (10 orderings) on C over the mapped terminal set, plus the SPT seed; verify and expand: a path in C expands to a real node path by inserting, for each contracted hop (A→B), the cheapest real priced edge from any node in A to any node in B, and inside each SCC a free directed path (BFS on F) between the entry and exit nodes. (4) Feed expanded per-dst paths through the existing `sp_cost`/`local_search` machinery; commit the best. Validity: every emitted hop is a real edge of `h`; per-dst Dijkstra fallback still covers any dst whose expansion fails, so all dsts always receive a path.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is unconditional free traversal inside zero-cost SCCs; whenever any incumbent path uses a priced edge whose endpoints lie in one free SCC (or a priced edge replaceable by a free intra-SCC detour), the contracted solution strictly lowers raw `total_cost` below 627.12, hence raises `combined_score` above 0.001592 — falsifiable by rerunning the same 5 configs.
